segments.t: At the agency office in Paris, Mathias's wife Catherine arrives unexpectedly, hoping to travel down to Cannes to surprise her husband. Desperate to book a ticket when all flights are sold out, Catherine turns to Noemie, unaware that the assistant must sacrifice her own secret ticket. Listen to the scene in French first.
Bonjour, Noémie, vous partez?
Vous rejoignez Mathias à Cannes?
Je veux lui faire la surprise!
J'ai besoin de son programme.
Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
Mais tout est complet aujourd'hui.
Les choses vont beaucoup mieux entre nous.
Je vais imprimer le programme de Mathias.
Tous les vols sont complets, madame.
Et pour le train?
Une place reste dans le train de nuit.
Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
Merci pour votre aide précieuse.
Mathias ne peut pas se passer de toi.
Let's walk through the conversation step by step.
Bonjour, Noémie, vous partez?
'Hello, Noemie, are you leaving?' Catherine greets Mathias's dedicated assistant in the office. The polite inquiry notices her packed bags.
Vous rejoignez Mathias à Cannes?
'Are you joining Mathias in Cannes?' Catherine asks about Mathias's schedule at the festival. The proper noun phrase specifies the film festival city.
Je veux lui faire la surprise!
'I want to surprise him!' Mathias's wife reveals her secret romantic plan. The infinitive verb expresses her spontaneous intention.
J'ai besoin de son programme.
'I need his schedule.' Catherine asks for her husband's festival agenda. The fixed idiomatic expression denotes necessity.
Vous pourriez me réserver un vol?
'Could you book a flight for me?' She requests assistant help with travel bookings. The polite conditional verb asks for a booking service.
Mais tout est complet aujourd'hui.
'But everything is fully booked today.' Noemie explains that festival flights are unavailable. The predicate adjective describes total lack of seats.
Les choses vont beaucoup mieux entre nous.
'Things are going much better between us.' Catherine confides that their marital relationship has improved. The adverbial comparative emphasizes positive change.
Je vais imprimer le programme de Mathias.
'I will print Mathias's schedule.' Noemie cooperates despite her hidden affair with Mathias. The near-future verb form indicates immediate action.
Tous les vols sont complets, madame.
'All flights are fully booked, madam.' She confirms the complete lack of airplane seats. The universal quantifier emphasizes zero availability.
Et pour le train?
'What about the train?' Catherine refuses to give up on traveling down south. The elliptical question proposes a rail alternative.
Une place reste dans le train de nuit.
'One seat remains on the night train.' Noemie reluctantly gives up her own reserved sleeper berth. The noun phrase designates the overnight rail service.
Je peux lui apporter des croissants!
'I can bring him croissants!' Catherine excitedly imagines breakfast with her husband. The modal verb introduces a cheerful romantic gesture.
Tu es mon sauveur, Noémie!
'You are my savior, Noemie!' Catherine warmly hugs the conflicted assistant. The predicate noun expresses enthusiastic gratitude.
Merci pour votre aide précieuse.
'Thank you for your valuable help.' She expresses heartfelt appreciation for the booking. The polite formula acknowledges office support.
Mathias ne peut pas se passer de toi.

'Mathias cannot manage without you.' Catherine praises Noemie's indispensable role, unaware of their secret romance. The idiomatic verb phrase denotes complete reliance. Now listen to the whole scene again at normal speed, and see how much more you catch.

Heartbroken and conflicted, Noemie gives up her own overnight train ticket so that Mathias's wife can surprise him in Cannes. Listen to the conversation once more in French.
Bon voyage à Cannes, madame.
